# Lenz 0.0.23 beta

This release makes Lenz find an installed `git` when it is started from the desktop (PR #74).

- **Git from the desktop.** An app started from Finder on macOS sees only `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, so Lenz ran Apple's `git` stub and asked for the Command Line Tools even when Homebrew's git was installed. Lenz now runs the first `git` on its `PATH`, then one in the install folders a desktop launch cannot see: Homebrew's and MacPorts' prefixes and the Command Line Tools' own `git` on macOS, `/usr/local/bin` and Homebrew's `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin` on Linux.
- Apple's `/usr/bin/git` stub runs only when the Command Line Tools are installed. A `git` older than 2.30, or one that cannot be run, is skipped for the next.
- Hooks and helpers such as `git lfs` find the same install: commands you start, and network commands, put its folder first on `PATH`.
- `LENZ_GIT` names an absolute path to the `git` to run instead.

## Validation

The release commit passes the full local Linux gate and `scripts/perf-check.sh`. Native macOS interaction, including a Finder launch, remains unverified. Native package build/signature and CLI checks are separate from interactive validation. macOS packages are ad-hoc signed.

Keep all five executables together. Verify the matching `.sha256` sidecar before installation.

[Changes since 0.0.22](https://github.com/aantoniadis/lenz/compare/v0.0.22...v0.0.23).
